newsitem.title: USA: Alaska proposes $1 mln reward to draw Japan flights.
newsitem.headline: Alaska proposes $1 mln reward to draw Japan flights.

text.p: In an effort to boost tourism, Gov. Tony Knowles on Thursday proposed a $1 million reward to the first airline to establish regular direct passenger service between Japan and Alaska.
The reward -- in cash, landing-fee credits or other forms -- would help convince international carriers that Alaska is a worthwhile year-round passenger destination, Knowles said in a speech.

Direct passenger service between Japan and Alaska used to be a staple for airlines that used Anchorage as a refueling stop during the Cold War. But the opening of shorter routes over Siberia and development of new long-range aircraft have allowed international carriers to skip Alaska.
Passenger flights between Alaska and Japan are now routed through Seattle or Seoul, extending to up to 16 hours what would be a six- or seven-hour flight, Knowles said.

He said carriers likely to be interested in the reward include Northwest Airlines, All Nippon Airways and Japan Air Lines, which has a long history of Alaska operations. All the carriers have international cargo operations in Anchorage.
The incentive plan requires approval by the Republican-led state legislature.
